This confirms the single-selection branch (the one modified by the fix) was introduced here, with no null-check on `value` — that gap is exactly what commit `944abee60` later fixes by wrapping the block in `if (value != null) { ... }`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b1940a88bf7e10bc2ec8dcc19d5120ffd98d2690

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the file's history with `git log -p --follow` on `SavedHqlExportToCSV.java` and searched for the surrounding code pattern (`lookupValue`, `getParameter(option.name())`) across all historical diffs to find where the exact block modified by the fix was first introduced.

(2) Commit `b1940a88b` ("Wed Mar 1 17:24:57 2017") added the `for (SavedHQL.Option option: ...)` loop, including the `else` branch for single-selection options:
```java
String value = helper.getParameter(option.name());
SavedHQLInterface.IdValue v = new SavedHQLInterface.IdValue();
v.setValue(option.name());
Long id = option.lookupValue(context.getUser(), value);
...
```
This is the exact code (same structure, same variable names) that the fix commit `944abee60` wraps in `if (value != null) { ... }`. The original code never checked whether `value` (the request parameter) was null before passing it to `option.lookupValue(...)` and `Long.valueOf(value)`, and before unconditionally calling `params.add(v)` — adding a spurious empty-valued parameter whenever the request parameter for that option was absent.

(3) The diff of `b1940a88b` shows this block being added fresh (all `+` lines, no prior equivalent code existed), and no intermediate commit between `b1940a88b` and `944abee60` touched this null-check logic (confirmed via the `git log -p` output showing the next relevant commits were unrelated refactors). This is a straightforward, high-confidence match — the fix is a minimal, targeted patch (add a null guard) to code whose origin is unambiguous in the history.
